title: Tomato Paste, Canned, No Salt Added

content.title: About
content.content: Tomato paste, canned without added salt, is a concentrated product made from ripe tomatoes that have been cooked down and sealed in glass or metal jars. It has a deep tomato flavor, aromatic intensity, and a thick texture, making it ideal for sauces, soups, and a variety of dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato paste retains over 90 % of the original tomato water, but the cooking process intensifies its taste and aroma.
Canning without salt allows the paste to be used in low‑sodium and diet‑friendly recipes.
Tomatoes used for paste are often grown in greenhouses, ensuring consistent quality year‑round.
Tomato paste serves as a base for many traditional dishes, from Italian marinara to Mexican salsa.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The paste provides vitamin B6, niacin, and folate, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Although some vitamin C is lost during heat processing, the paste still retains a notable amount, helping to boost immunity.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Tomato paste contains potassium, magnesium, and iron, contributing to normal muscle and blood function.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: The absence of added salt makes it suitable for people monitoring their sodium intake.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to digestive upset.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of tomato paste can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some manufacturers add preservatives such as potassium sorbate; those sensitive should check the label.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add tomato paste to sauces, stews, soups, pizza, marinades, and vegetable casseroles. Dilute with water or broth as needed, and enhance flavor with herbs, spices, and a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the paste in the refrigerator in an airtight container and use within 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odors, or other signs of spoilage.
